name: Citrus-Basil Syrup
description:
A sugar-based syrup infused with fresh basil leaves and citrus juice or zest. It is primarily used to add herbal and acidic notes to non-alcoholic beverages, mocktails, and mixed drinks. The preparation involves steeping the herbs in a simple syrup base.

### Instructions
- 1 cup water
- 1 cup white sugar
- 1 1/2-inch piece of Buddha’s hand citron, peeled and diced (use the “fingers,” including the flesh)
- 1 1/2 to 2 dried makrut lime leaves
- 1 ounce lemon juice
- 2 to 3 basil leaves
- peel of 1 lime, pith removed

Add water and sugar to a small saucepan over low heat, stirring to incorporate. Raise heat to medium, and add the Buddha’s hand, lime leaves and lemon juice. Bring to a boil. Reduce the temperature to low and add the basil. Cover the syrup and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes. (Let it steep longer, off heat, if you prefer a stronger basil flavor.) Remove from the stove and add the lime peel. Allow the syrup to cool, then strain into a nonreactive container. Keeps, refrigerated, for up to 3 weeks.

If you cannot obtain Buddha’s hand, combine 5 ounces of lemon juice, 3 ounces of water and 1 whole lemon sliced into wheels, and following the recipe as directed.
